subject: Observability: fine-grain route economics & latency telemetry sync
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability: fine-grain route economics & latency telemetry sync

Hi team,

Following up from last week's customer briefing with Acme Analytics — they pushed back on our console story for route-level economics. Specifically they want:

- Per-route token cost broken down by model variant (e.g., gpt-x-16k vs gpt-x-8k) and by generation vs. embedding tokens.
- Tail latency percentiles (p95/p99) for each route with time-of-day heatmaps and the ability to filter by tenant/namespace.
- A way to mark routes as "billable" vs "non-billable" in the view so finance can map to contracts.
- Alerting triggers when route cost deviates from historical baseline (>20% week-over-week) or when p99 > SLO.

I sketched a quick wireframe (attached) and exported a small sample of route cost attribution (sample-route-costs.csv) so we can see edge cases where batching/kv-cache makes per-request attribution noisy.

Key business constraints: Acme is evaluating Redwood vs competitor X; their procurement lead flagged console visibility as a gating item before procurement signs. Marcus flagged this as deal-impacting (see thread cc).

Questions for engineering/observability:
1) How feasible is extracting model-variant token split at per-route granularity in our ingestion/metric pipeline?
2) Estimated infra cost of maintaining p99 heatmaps and tenant filters for the last 90 days?
3) Quick mitigation: can we surface an approximation today (sampled breakdown + clear caveats) while we build the definitive view?

Can we aim to get a quick feasibility note by EOD tomorrow and a proposed implementation timeline by Friday?

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Product Manager, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: fine-grain route economics & latency telemetry sync

On Tue, 18 May 2027 at 09:12, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following up from last week's customer briefing with Acme Analytics — they pushed back on our console story for route-level economics.

Thanks for the context and the wireframe, Logan. Quick thoughts after a rapid read and a quick sync with the telemetry team:

- Model-variant token split: we already tag requests with the model_id used for the served inference. Generational vs embedding token attribution is the tricky bit — embeddings currently flow through a separate endpoint, so those tokens are already partitioned by endpoint, but for generation calls we don't separately record "prompt vs completion" tokens at route attribution time unless we hook into the request lifecycle early (and that adds some extra E2E overhead).

- Sampling approach: absolutely doable as a stop-gap. We can emit a sampled event (1:50) capturing prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/model_id/route_id and run a small daily job to expand to expected totals. Caveat: sampling hides short-lived tail latency spikes which customers care about.

- p99 heatmaps & tenant filtering: we have p99 calculation pipelines (Prometheus->long-term metrics store) but not yet tiled heatmaps baked into the console. Building the UI + precomputed aggregates for 90 days will add storage and compute costs; rough order-of-magnitude: an additional ~350GB of compressed metrics storage + extra nightly aggregation jobs (~2-3 vCPUs).

- Billable flag: simple metadata change in the route config schema (boolean) — low effort but needs migration tooling for existing routes.

I'll put together a short feasibility doc with options (sampling vs full instrumentation) and estimated timelines. For a low-risk MVP we can:
A) Ship sampled cost splits + route billable flag + per-route p95/p99 for last 30 days (UI values derived from preaggregates) in ~6 weeks.
B) Full fidelity (per-request token split + 90 day tileable heatmaps) would be ~12-14 weeks and requires a short migration and additional infra budget.

I'll draft the doc and share a link later today.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Engineering Lead, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Observability: fine-grain route economics & latency telemetry sync

Looping in a bit of customer context from Acme — they currently run multiple internal tenants and their procurement lead specifically asked for:

- Ability to export per-route month-to-month cost breakdown for finance reviews.
- Programmatic access (CSV/CSV via API) so they can ingest into their internal chargeback system.
- A short window (two weeks) for final demo before they commit to the POC phase.

If the MVP (sampling + billable flag + p95/p99 last 30d) is feasible in 6 weeks, that might work, but they want to see demo artifacts earlier — even a static dashboard or a pre-rendered sample in the console would help.

As a sales ask: can we get a "show-and-tell" dataset and a screenshot by May 27th? That gives us time to present to their procurement folks on June 1st.

Marcus
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: fine-grain route economics & latency telemetry sync

Thanks — pulled the thread into a short playbook and a rough implementation plan (attached to JIRA-INF-1427). Summary:

Action items & owners:
- Grace: Draft feasibility doc + sampling vs full instrumentation decision matrix (ETA: 2027-05-21 EOD).
- Monica: Prototype data export pipeline (CSV) using sampled events and produce a demo CSV and a static console screenshot (ETA: 2027-05-25).
- Logan: Finalize customer-facing wireframe and list of contracts that need billable flag mapping (ETA: 2027-05-22).
- Marcus: Coordinate Acme procurement dates and confirm June 1 demo slot (ETA: 2027-05-24).

Risks called out:
- Sampling will under-represent rare but expensive edge cases (large completions). Call out this caveat prominently in the demo.
- Storage/compute incremental cost for 90-day preaggregates will need a ticket to infra budget (est. $Xk/month — placeholder in the JIRA ticket).

I'll attach the prototype CSV and a static screenshot to the Jira ticket once the job runs. If everyone agrees on the timeline, I'll convert these items into a short roadmap and update the sprint board.

Monica
Observability PM
Redwood Inference
